newsitem.title: UK: EU's Brittan derides Eurosceptics over Euro.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan derides Eurosceptics over Euro.

text.p: Sir Leon Brittan, Britain's senior European Commissioner, said on Friday that Eurosceptics in the ruling Conservative party were ridiculous to condemn plans for a single currency.

"It is not a question of handing power to the "boys in Brussels'. It is a question of an independent central bank which would not be controlled by the boys from Brussels in any way," he told BBC Radio.
Prime Minister John Major, battling to unite his fractious Conservative Party before fighting an election, has virtually ruled out Britain joining a European single currency in 1999.

"It is very unlikely, though not impossible, that the single currency itself could proceed safely on January 1,1999," Major told parliament on Thursday as he sought to win over Eurosceptics who fear Brussels is eroding national sovereignty.
Attacking Eurosceptic fears, Brittan said: "I think it is ridiculous to reject something that is very much in line with Conservative economic policy just because it comes from Brussels."
"This is not some irrational headlong flight to federalism. It is in fact a specific project designed to help jobs and reduce interest rates," he added.
